purpose: Data for a blog post: how far jsse has come since 2026-03-17 (compat + perf), vs Node, Boa, engine262.

jsse-current.note: 083746f is the v0.8.1 release commit: version-bump/changelog only on top of 077e4ec (no source changes).

jsse-current-bytecode.note: Bytecode compiler + VM for eligible functions; experimental, off by default.

engine262.version: 0.0.1 (package.json; built from GitHub main at run time)

toolchains.local_laptop_builds: rustc 1.98.0 (88d9e12ae 2026-08-18) for both jsse-current and jsse-mar17 (test262 runs)
toolchains.buildbox3_builds: rustc 1.100.0-nightly (330d31712 2026-09-17) for both jsse-current and jsse-mar17 (micro-benchmarks and JetStream)

hosts.test262_runs: ravenwing (laptop): AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370, 24 threads, Arch Linux; shared interactive desktop with variable load
hosts.perf_runs: buildbox3: AMD EPYC 7501 32-Core, 61 CPUs, Debian 12 (glibc 2.36), Linux 6.1.0-53; shared build machine (another user's RISC-V LNT jobs were running, baseline loadavg ~1.2-1.7)

test262.runner: scripts/run-test262.py (default suite: language, built-ins, annexB, intl402; each test run in sloppy and strict where applicable)

engine262.note: Estimate from a 10% per-directory random sample, not the full suite; CI is a naive binomial (Wilson) interval that ignores clustering by directory.

protocol.statistic: median wall-clock seconds per process invocation (includes engine startup)

bench_array.note: mar17 hit the 120s timeout; true speedup is at least this

jetstream.checkout: WebKit/JetStream c603c04db8505477867974a69789309ded2cc948 (assets decompressed with npm run decompress)

march_10_2026_three_engine_test262.suite: 91,986 scenarios (older test262 revision; NOT directly comparable to the 99,911-scenario suite above)

may_2026_head_vs_march_17.summary: JetStream 19/48 -> 26/48 passing; geomean speedup 1.92x on 19 common workloads; test262 wall time 4.73x faster (828.85s vs 175.2s).

caveats: test262: all engines ran the same checkout (aae8cf6, 99,911 scenarios) with the same runner and 120s timeout, so jsse-mar17's 98.96% is against TODAY's suite; its 1,039 failures are mostly features added after March 17 (Iterator helpers, Promise.allKeyed/allSettledKeyed, immutable ArrayBuffer, Atomics.waitAsync, AsyncDisposableStack, Temporal gaps), not regressions.
test262 was run on a shared interactive laptop with variable load: pass/fail counts are unaffected, but per-test timing stats (sum_of_per_test_wall_s etc.) are indicative only and run at -j 12.

Node: 830 module scenarios are skipped by the adapter (pass_rate_of_run 96.24% vs 95.44% of all scenarios), and the Node adapter uses a basic $262.agent prelude, so some Atomics/agent failures are adapter limitations rather than pure V8 conformance. Node runs under a larger address-space limit than jsse/boa (V8 needs it).
engine262: only a seeded 10% per-directory sample (seed 42) was run because a full run is impractically slow; treat its pass rate as an estimate.
Boa: run through its CLI with the harness inlined into the script; syntax-error (negative) tests are detected by a 'SyntaxError' substring in stderr.

Micro-benchmarks are tiny scripts timed per process (5 runs, median, includes engine startup). Node's ~0.1s numbers are largely startup floor, so slowdown-vs-node ratios are not meaningful as steady-state JIT comparisons. Timeouts (120s) are censored: engine262 timed out on bench_loop, bench_fib, bench_closures and bench_opmix; jsse-mar17 timed out on bench_array, so its speedup entry is a lower bound.

Perf runs (micro-benchmarks, JetStream) were done on buildbox3, a SHARED build machine: another user's RISC-V LNT jobs were running throughout (baseline loadavg ~1.2-1.7). The micro-benchmark run passed the 1.5 idle gate (loadavg 1.19 at start); JetStream was run with --no-idle-gate. Both jsse builds were built with the same toolchain on each host.
The perf runs used commit 083746f (the v0.8.1 release commit) while test262 runs used 077e4ec; 083746f only changes version/changelog files on top of 077e4ec.

JetStream: run with the project's runner (scripts/run-jetstream.py, --iterations 1, 120s timeout, 3 repeats, pinned JetStream c603c04), NOT JetStream's own driver, and with 1 iteration instead of the default iteration counts. Scores are therefore only meaningful as relative comparisons between the jsse builds, not comparable to published JetStream scores.

JetStream errors are not root-caused. Captured stderr suggests a mix: 'self is not defined' (bigint-paillier) looks like a host-API gap in the runner, while 'Generator is already running' (lazy-collections), 'tokenCount ... is invalid' (js-tokens), a large-number formatting mismatch in OfflineAssembler, a validatorjs assertion and a 'not a function' TypeError in cdjs look like possible engine bugs worth follow-up. 'no JSON output' failures are async workloads that were not investigated.
The --bytecode VM is experimental and off by default; it only affects functions eligible for compilation, so its effect is workload dependent (largest on bench_opmix).

Earlier aborted attempts (a laptop micro-benchmark run under load, and JetStream runs with default iteration counts, missing decompressed assets and a clobbered /tmp on buildbox3) were discarded and are not included in any number here.

reproduction.micro_benchmarks: benchmarks/scripts/bench_*.js, median of 5 process runs per engine
